title: 2025 PB #2: Two Identical Balls A And B
content:
Two identical balls A and B are aimed at each 
other and roll off the edges of two identical 
horizontal tabletops at exactly the same 
time. Each ball has sufficient velocity to land 
under the opposite table, but ball B has a 
greater initial velocity than ball A. What will 
happen as they fall? 
a. Ball B will pass over the top of ball A as they fall. 
b. Ball A will pass over the top of ball B as they fall. 
c. The two balls will collide as they fall. 
d. The two balls may collide only if their velocities are exactly the right values. 
e. Ball B will hit the floor before ball A.
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing gravitation & celestial.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
The force of gravity acts equally on both balls, causing them to accelerate 
toward the floor at the same rate, regardless of their initial horizontal velocities.
steps:
1. The force of gravity acts equally on both balls, causing them to accelerate 
toward the floor at the same rate, regardless of their initial horizontal velocities.
2. Because they were initially "aimed" at each other, they will collide.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Gravitation & Celestial problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2025 PB #27: A Block Of Wood Is Given

A block of wood is given a certain speed at the bottom of a rough ramp. The block slides 
a certain distance up the ramp and returns to the point from which it was launched. Let tup 
represent the time it takes the block to travel up the ramp to its highest point and tdown 
represent the time it takes the block to travel down the ramp to the bottom. Let aup 
represent the magnitude of the block's acceleration while traveling up the ramp and adown 
represent the block's acceleration while traveling down the ramp. Which of the following 
correctly compares these quantities?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing gravitation & celestial.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: When going up, friction and gravity act in the same direction, opposing motion.
steps: 1. When going up, friction and gravity act in the same direction, opposing motion.

2. When going down, friction opposes motion, while gravity acts in the direction of 
motion.
3. Therefore, aup>adown.

4. Since the distance is the same and aup>adown, 
then tup<tdown.

title: 2025 PB #38: Which Of The Following Statements About
content:
Which of the following statements about the electric field inside a charged conductor at 
electrostatic equilibrium is true?

options.text:
The strength increases uniformly with the distance from the center of the 
conductor.

The strength decreases uniformly with the distance from the center of the 
conductor.
The strength is a uniform, non-zero value everywhere.
The strength varies randomly from point to point.

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing electrostatics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
When a conductor is charged, the free charges within it redistribute themselves 
until the electric field inside the conductor is zero.
steps:
1. When a conductor is charged, the free charges within it redistribute themselves 
until the electric field inside the conductor is zero.

2. If there were a non-zero 
electric field inside the conductor, the free charges would experience a force and 
move, which would contradict the state of electrostatic equilibrium.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Electrostatics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2025 PB #49: Point Charges Q And Q Are
content:
Point charges +q and -q are fixed in place on the x-axis at x = +d and x = -d, respectively. 
At x = 0, their net electric field __________ and their total electric potential __________. 
 
 Net electric field Total electric potential

options.text: points in the positive x-direction is positive
points in the negative x-direction is negative
points in the positive x-direction is zero
points in the negative x-direction is zero

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing electrostatics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
The electric field due to a positive charge points away from the charge, while the 
electric field due to a negative charge points towards the charge.
steps:
1. The electric field due to a positive charge points away from the charge, while the 
electric field due to a negative charge points towards the charge.

2. At x=0, the 
electric fields from both charges have equal magnitude but opposite directions 
and thus cancel out, resulting in a net electric field of zero.

3. At x=0, the distances 
from both charges are equal and the potential from one charge is positive, while 
the potential from the other charge is negative.

4. These two potentials are equal in 
magnitude, so their sum is zero.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Electrostatics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2024 PB #24: An Ideal Gas Undergoes An Isothermal
content:
An ideal gas undergoes an isothermal process. Which of the following statements about 
the change in internal energy (U) for the gas and heat (Q) is true during this process?

options.text: U is zero, and Q is zero.
U is zero, and Q is not zero.
U is not zero, and Q is zero.
U is not zero, and Q is not zero, but they are not equal.
U is not zero, and Q is not zero, and they are equal.

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing thermodynamics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: In an isothermal process, the temperature of the gas remains constant.
steps: 1. In an isothermal process, the temperature of the gas remains constant.

2. Since 
internal energy, U, of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature, and the 
temperature is constant throughout the process, the change in internal energy U 
is zero.

3. However, heat, Q, can still be transferred to or from the gas during the 
process.
4. This transfer of heat is necessary to maintain the constant temperature.
5. Therefore, Q is not zero.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Thermodynamics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2024 PB #39: An Increase In The Average Speed
content:
An increase in the average speed of the molecules of a gas confined in a rigid cylinder 
will correspond to an…

options.text: increase in the temperature of the gas only.
increase in the pressure of the gas only.
increase in both the temperature and the pressure of the gas.
increase in the temperature of the gas and a decrease in its pressure.
increase in the pressure of the gas and a decrease in its temperature.

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing thermodynamics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
When the average speed of the gas molecules increases, the kinetic energy of the 
molecules also increases.
steps:
1. When the average speed of the gas molecules increases, the kinetic energy of the 
molecules also increases.

2. This corresponds to an increase in the temperature of 
the gas.

3. According to the ideal gas law (PV = nRT), when the temperature of a 
gas increases while the volume remains constant (as in the case of a rigid 
cylinder), the pressure of the gas also increases.

4. Therefore, both the temperature 
and the pressure of the gas increase when the average speed of the gas molecules 
increases.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Thermodynamics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2024 PB #46: A Small Object Is Placed In
content:
A small object is placed in front of a concave mirror 
and to the left of the center of curvature at point P in 
the picture. As the object is moved from point P to 
point Q, the size of the image produced will …

options.text: first increase, then decrease and then increase again.

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing waves & optics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
As the object is moved from point P to point Q, the size of the image 
produced by the concave mirror will initially increase.
steps:
1. As the object is moved from point P to point Q, the size of the image 
produced by the concave mirror will initially increase.

2. This is because the object 
moves closer to the focal point of the mirror, resulting in the image moving 
further away from the mirror and becoming larger.

3. However, as the object moves 
past the focal point and closer to the mirror, the image size will then decrease.

4. At 
this point, the image will become larger than the object, virtual, and erect.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Waves & Optics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2023 PB #49: A Circuit Consists Of A Resistor
content:
A circuit consists of a resistor, capacitor, and inductor connected in series to an AC 
source. As the source frequency increases, the current in the circuit decreases. Which 
statement about the circuit is NOT correct as the source frequency increases?

options.text: The impedance of the circuit increases.
The circuit is said to become more capacitive than inductive.
The phase angle for the circuit becomes more positive.
The total power from the source decreases

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
Inductors have a voltage related to change… as driving frequency increases, the 
inductor reacts more strongly.
steps:
1. Inductors have a voltage related to change… as driving frequency increases, the 
inductor reacts more strongly.
2. Hence, the circuit is said to be more inductive.

3. From AC circuit theory, a higher frequency increases the inductive reactance and 
makes the phase angle more positive.

4. As the reactance increases, the impedance 
must be increasing as the current decreases, and the current decreases, so does the 
power associated with the resistor (and hence the source).
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Circuits & Electricity problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2023 PB #50: An Electron E Is Moving And
content:
An electron (e-) is moving and has kinetic energy of 1.00 MeV. It makes a head-on 
collision with a positron (e+) that is at rest. In the collision the two particles annihilate 
each other and are replaced by two photons (γ ) of equal energy, each traveling at angles 
θ to the electron's original direction of motion. The reaction is e- + e+ → 2γ. Determine 
the angle of emission θ of each photon.
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing momentum & collisions.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
The moving electron has momentum, p, along the positive x-axis and kinetic 
energy, K.
steps:
1. The moving electron has momentum, p, along the positive x-axis and kinetic 
energy, K.

2. The total energy, E, of the electron and the stationary positron before 
the collision is E = K + 2mc2 = 2.022 MeV.

3. The two photons emerge from the 
collision each with energy Eγ = ½ E = 1.011 MeV as given by conservation of 
energy, and each with magnitude of momentum pγ = Eγ/c = 1.011 MeV/c.

4. The 
momentum vectors of the photons make angles ±θ with the x-axis.

5. Conservation 
of momentum in the x-direction is p = 2pγ cos θ from which θ = 45.3o.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Momentum & Collisions problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2021 PB #47: In An Ideal Lc Circuit What

in the inductor and all of the energy being stored in the capacitor?

After one full period of oscillation has passed

Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
Since there is no resistance in the circuit, no energy is lost through Joule heating; thus, 
the maximum energy stored in the capacitor is equal to the maximum energy stored at a 
later time in the inductor.

the maximum energy stored in the capacitor is equal to the maximum energy stored at a 
later time in the inductor.

the end of a spring.

3. Energy is transferred back and forth between the mass, which has 
kinetic energy and the spring which has potential energy.

title: 2019 PB #24: The Capacitor Is Initially Uncharged Which
content:
The capacitor is initially uncharged. Which of the following choices best represents the current at 
Point X immediately after the switch is closed?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
Because there is no charge across the capacitor, there is no potential difference across 
the capacitor.
steps:
1. Because there is no charge across the capacitor, there is no potential difference across 
the capacitor.

2. Therefore, the potential at the junction between the 100  resistor and 
the 300  resistor is the same as the potential at the junction between the 400  
resistor and the 200  resistor.

3. As a result, the 100 ohm and 400 ohm resistors can be 
treated as a parallel combination connected in series to the parallel combination of the 
300  and 200  resistors.

4. This gives an equivalent resistance of 200  and a total 
current of 60 mA.

5. The potential difference across the top two resistors must be equal 
and their total current must add to 60 mA, resulting in a currents of 48 mA and 12 mA in 
the 100  and 400  resistors, respectively.

6. Using the same reasoning, the currents in 
the 300  and 400  resistors are 24 mA and 36 mA, respectively.

7. Using the junction to 
the left of the capacitor: I100 = Ix + I300, 48 mA = 24 mA + Ix.
8. Ix = 24 mA
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Circuits & Electricity problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2019 PB #25: If The Capacitor Has A Capacitance
content:

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
At steady‐state, no charge flows to or from the capacitor, so any current through the 
100  resistor continues to the 300  resistor.
steps:
1. At steady‐state, no charge flows to or from the capacitor, so any current through the 
100  resistor continues to the 300  resistor.

2. The same is true for the 400  resistor 
and the 200  resistor.

3. The potential drops across the 100  and 300  resistor must 
total 12 V.

4. Because the current is the same in these resistors, the voltage drops are 
proportional to the resistances: 3 V for the 100  and 9 V for the 300 .

5. By the same 
reasoning, the voltage drops across the 400 ohm and 200 ohm are 8 V and 4 V 
respectively.

6. The resulting potential difference between the junction to the left of the 
capacitor and the junction to the right of the capacitor is 5 V.

7. Using Q = 
CΔV = (15 μF)(5 V), gives 75 μC.

title: 2017 PB #31: A Solid Cylinder Rolls Without Slipping
content:
A solid cylinder rolls without slipping on a rough inclined plane. Which one of the following choices best 
represents the type and direction of friction (if any) acting on the cylinder as it rolls up the incline?

options.text: Static friction directed up the incline
Kinetic friction directed up the incline
Kinetic friction directed down the incline
Static friction directed down the incline

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing rotational motion.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
… Since the object is rolling without slipping, any friction would have to be static on the incline 
(there is no relative motion between cylinder and surface).
steps:
1. … Since the object is rolling without slipping, any friction would have to be static on the incline 
(there is no relative motion between cylinder and surface).

2. As for the direction, one notes that if 
the friction acts down the incline (as one might suspect being "opposite to the motion"), this 
would cause the speed of the object to decrease, but it also would cause an increase in the 
rotational speed of the object.

3. The torque from the center of the cylinder would make the object 
spin faster and faster which cannot happen.

4. Consequently, in order to slow the rotation, the 
friction must be pointing up the incline!
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Rotational Motion problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2017 PB #33: Two Long Wires Are Fixed In
content:
Two long wires are fixed in space so that the conventional current in the left wire (2 𝐴) comes out of 
the plane of the page and the conventional current in the right wire (3 𝐴) goes into the plane of the 
page. In which Region(s) is there a place on the x-axis (aside from infinity) at which the magnetic field 
is equal to zero from these currents?

options.text: In both Regions I and II
In both Regions I and III
In both Regions II and III

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
… From the right-hand rule, the thumb points along the direction of current and the right 
fingers wrap in the sense of the magnetic field lines.
steps:
1. … From the right-hand rule, the thumb points along the direction of current and the right 
fingers wrap in the sense of the magnetic field lines.

2. Consequently, for the 2-A current, the field 
points downward anywhere to the left of the wire and upward anywhere to the right of the wire on 
the x-axis.

3. Likewise, the 3-A current produces fields that point downward anywhere to the right 
of the wire and upward everywhere to the left of the wire.

4. To have no total field, the individual 
magnetic fields must cancel (point in opposite directions) and that only occurs in Regions I and 
III.

5. However, since points in Region III always are closer to the larger current, there is no way 

for the smaller current, acting from further away, to cancel the field from the larger current.

6. The 
only way the fields can cancel is if the larger current is acting from a greater distance which 
corresponds to a location in Region I.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Circuits & Electricity problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2016 PB #43: A Uniform Beam Connected To A
content:
A uniform beam connected to a wall at the hinge is in static equilibrium as shown. The cable connected 
to the beam is massless. What are the directions of the horizontal and vertical components of force acting 
at the pivot on the beam? 
 
 Horizontal component Vertical component

options.text: It cannot be determined It cannot be determined

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing rotational motion.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
… As the object is in static equilibrium, the sum of forces and the 
sum of torques must be zero.
steps:
1. … As the object is in static equilibrium, the sum of forces and the 
sum of torques must be zero.

2. The force from the cable is upward and 
rightward.

3. Because the gravitational force is downward, the pivot 
must be providing a force to the left in order to cancel the rightward 
force from the cable.

4. As for the vertical component, by choosing an 
axis of rotation through the direction of the gravitational force at the 
vertical location of the pivot, the only non-zero torques are from the 
cable and the vertical component of the pivot force.

5. As the torque 
from the cable would be oriented counterclockwise from this axis of rotation, the vertical force at the 
pivot needs to provide a clockwise torque.
6. This is possible only if that vertical component is upward.

content:
Two small loops of wire are located close to a wire with conventional current directed up 
the page. A scientist then moves the loops away from the current as shown. What is the 
orientation of the conventional current in each loop while this occurs? 
 
 Left loop Right loop

steps: 1. … Lenz's Law is required to answer this question.

2. The magnetic field associated with the long wire 
is into the page to the right of the wire and out of the page to the left of the wire.

right is moved away, there are weaker field lines penetrating into the loop.

plane through the interior of the loop.

title: 2014 PB #34: Two Circular Loops Of Resistive Wire
content:
Two circular loops of resistive wire are placed next to each other as in the figure. The circular loop on 
the left is connected to a constant voltage source 𝑉. The resistance of this loop is increasing linearly 
with time. As the resistance is changing, what is the direction of the magnetic field at point P (the 
center of the left-hand loop) and what is the orientation of the conventional current in the right-hand 
loop (as viewed in the figure from above)? 
 
 Magnetic Field Direction Current Orientation

options.text: Into the plane of the page Counterclockwise
Into the plane of the page Clockwise
Out of the plane of the page Counterclockwise
Out of the plane of the page Clockwise
There is no field There is no current

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary:
… By a right-hand rule, the fingers curl in the direction of the conventional current (clockwise) and the 
right thumb points in the direction of the magnetic field at the center of the loop (into the plane).
steps:
1. … By a right-hand rule, the fingers curl in the direction of the conventional current (clockwise) and the 
right thumb points in the direction of the magnetic field at the center of the loop (into the plane).

2. Because 
magnetic field lines form closed loops, the field is directed out of the plane of the page inside the loop on 
the right.

3. Because the resistance of the left-hand circuit is increasing, the current in that loop is decreasing, 
thereby decreasing the magnetic field strength.

4. In the right-hand loop, since the field through the loop is 
decreasing in magnitude, induction occurs to reinforce the lost field.

5. This means from the right-hand rule 
that the fingers will curl counterclockwise around the loop to produce a magnetic field out of the plane, 
trying to replace the field lines that are being lost.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Circuits & Electricity problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.
